annotations.title: God wil circumciſe thy hart.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> Moſt true it is, that of our ſelues, without Gods grace none can kepe or fulfil the commandmentes. But he, whoſe hart God doth circumciſe, is therby made able to loue God with al his hart, and with al his ſoule. And except ſome hartes were thus circumciſed, and ſo made able to loue God aboue al, and conſequently their neighboures, God ſhould not performe his promiſe, that he wil circumciſe the hart of ſome.

notes.text: By grace men are made able to kepe Gods commandments

annotations.title: Is not aboue thee.
annotations.text: [1] VVhen thou art ſtirred vp, aſſiſted, and indued with Gods grace, [2]the commandment of God is not (then) aboue thee, nor farre of from thee, but very nere thee, in thy mouth (to confeſſe God, and his truth) and in thy hart, to do it. But you wil aske: How then cometh it to paſſe, that manie hauing receiued ſufficient grace, yet do not kepe Gods commandmentes? God him ſelf anſwereth: 15. That he hath ſet before thee life and good, and contrriwiſe death and euil; he inuiteth and helpeth, yet forceth thee not: he geueth thee powre & abilitie, helping and not deſtroying thy freewil, that thou maiſt loue our Lord thy God, walke in his wayes, and kepe his commandements. But if thy hart be auerted and (v. 17.) thou wilt not heare, thou shalt perish. Againe God inculcateth: 19. I cal for witneſſes heauen and earth, that I haue propoſed to you life and death, bleſſing and curſing. Chooſe therfore life &c. VVhat Doctor can teach more plainly the poſſibilitie of keeping Gods commandmentes; and frewil in man, then this text of holie Scripture?

notes.text: So the commandmentes are not impoſſible.
S. Aug. de nat. et grat. c. 69. et q. 54. in Deut. Theod. q. 38. in Deut. S. Cypr. l. 3. c. 52. ad Quir. S. Amb. in Pſal. 40.
